mutant.description: The control the face itself designates as the one that MUST be able to fail: S12-AC3's expired capability token. If the expired token were still accepted, the expiry would be configured and not effective -- which is the entire outcome FWD-12 names. The mutant is real elapsed time against a real exp claim, presented through the real edge: the SAME token, past its 300s TTL plus leeway, re-presented to the same endpoint.
mutant.expected: 401 on the second presentation of the same token, against a 200 on the first
mutant.observed: 200 ACCEPTED at 2026-09-09T19:14:26Z, then 401 REFUSED at 2026-09-09T19:19:51Z -- same token, same endpoint, 325 seconds apart. The pair discriminates: a gateway that ignored exp would have returned 200 twice, and a broken endpoint would have returned 401 twice.

determinism.method: Each wire claim was re-run rather than read once. The static-bearer acceptance control was run 3 times in consecutive seconds; the refusal controls were run in two independent forms (absent header, junk bearer); the reachability flip was measured on BOTH new endpoints, not one; and the pre/post edge reads were taken 45 minutes apart across the apply.
determinism.observed: Static bearer 200/200/200 at 19:22:33Z, 19:22:34Z, 19:22:36Z. Refusals 401 (no header) and 401 (junk bearer). Reachability after apply: /otp/token 401 server=uvicorn AND /ms/token 401 server=uvicorn, both flipped from 302 Server=awselb/2.0. ONE NON-DETERMINISM WAS OBSERVED AND IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED: the first run of the static-bearer control returned curl status 000 -- a connect/timeout sentinel, NOT an HTTP status and NOT a refusal. It was re-run rather than interpreted, and the three 200s above are that re-run.
